comparator.name: Bachelor Civil Engineering
comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–2027 ordinary cohort requirements; checked against the completed 7 October audit and current source retrieval on 8 October 2026
comparator.sourceNotes: The controlling 2026–2027 Civil Engineering Annex and September 2026 curriculum chart were verified in the completed 7 October audit. Their ordinary 2026-entry structure is 60+60+60=180. Current year-one Water en Techniek CTB1215-26 replaces the older Schone Watersystemen title/code. Formal Transport en planning CTB1420-25 governs the stale CTB1420-17 chart label. Bouwplaats 1 and 2 are each an aggregate 8 EC; their quarter subdivisions are not separately credited at 8 each. Year three is minor 30 + Surveying and Mapping CTB3310 4 + Urban Water and Environmental Engineering CTB3315 4 + Traffic and Transport Infrastructure CTB3325 4 + one Q3 deep-dive 4 + one Q4 design choice 4 + bachelor project CTB3000-16 10 = 60. Restricted options are instantiated by the first-listed eligible choice in each category: Climate Impacts and Engineering CTB3311 and Design of Water Treatment CTB3465, independently of UCR fit. The old unrestricted three-specialisation arrangement applies only to pre-2024 cohorts. The minor remains genuine choice and must not overlap selected degree/elective units. Fresh current programme-page retrieval corroborates the construction/water/transport identity; fresh formal Annex and chart downloads returned HTTP 502, so formal units, weights and visual verification are explicitly carried from the current-year 7 October audit, not claimed as new retrievals. During the separate UCR reassessment on 10 October 2026, the current formal Annex was successfully retrieved and its ordinary curriculum/choice tables (PDF pp.20–21) visually inspected. These corroborate the existing corrected requirements; the historical download-failure note above refers to 8 October. No programme route, restricted choice or EC value was changed.
components: Genuine choice allowance, subject to applicable approval and overlap rules.

core: Water, flood risk and climate-resilient infrastructure
Environmental systems, resources and sustainable material cycles
Mathematics, statistics and empirical infrastructure modelling
adjacent: Stakeholder needs and infrastructure lifecycle decisions

alternatives.label: Water systems, environmental science & modelling
alternatives.concept: Study water, flood risk, climate-resilient interventions, environmental resources and material cycles with substantive mathematical, statistical and empirical modelling. This is a related-fields response to the full Civil Engineering target; structural, fluid-mechanics, construction and transport formation remains visibly incomplete.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines environmental/water study with five mathematical courses and data/research tools; it is not labelled as full Civil Engineering.
progression: All workbook prerequisites, exact semester availability, 24 unique courses, PPD and six advanced courses passed. Sustainability and mathematical foundations precede advanced work; linear algebra precedes numerical/advanced mathematics. Earth observation, soils/aquifers and Living with Water require semester four, leaving one slot for Numerical Methods or Public Economics. Numerical Methods precedes Advanced Calculus. Linear Systems and Numerical Methods cannot both join those three environmental courses in that sole term; no unavailable course is inserted to conceal this timetable constraint. Social foundations precede contemporary theory in the second programme.

alternatives.label: Water resilience, public infrastructure & communities
alternatives.concept: Retain water and environmental science while examining stakeholder experiences, collective decisions, resource impacts and public-economic choices across infrastructure lifecycles.
alternatives.labelReason: The full curriculum replaces specialist mathematical/programming depth with qualitative/social and economic inquiry while retaining substantial environmental science.

Linear Systems and Numerical Methods cannot both join those three environmental courses in that sole term; no unavailable course is inserted to conceal this timetable constraint. Social foundations precede contemporary theory in the second programme.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ: programming, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability/statistics and advanced calculus are replaced by sociology, contemporary civil-society theory, qualitative research, introductory economics and public economics. These changes implement the evidenced stakeholder/lifecycle direction.

candidates.label: Stakeholder needs and infrastructure lifecycle decisions
Road, rail and waterway transport infrastructure

selection.assessment: Two distinct water/environmental responses pass all academic and mechanical gates. A structural/ground/underground concept cannot supply the absent engineering mechanics, foundation, steel/concrete and construction-design sequences; soils/aquifers fieldwork is not a substitute. A separate transport-infrastructure concept cannot supply road/rail engineering, transport-demand/traffic theory and engineering design; general data or optimisation methods would not establish that programme. Additional mathematical modelling is already substantive in the closest response. The unavailable Spatial Planning course was considered but not used.

blocks: Both directly study drainage, freshwater management and water infrastructure affecting inhabited regions; UCR adds governance and delta cases rather than the full urban-water engineering scope.
Both directly develop geospatial mapping and analysis; satellite/GIS methods do not reproduce all surveying and dimensional-control practice.
Aquifer mapping and freshwater-resource investigation directly address the groundwater part of hydrology; UCR does not reproduce the full surface-water/engineering-hydrology sequence.
Both directly study wastewater treatment and engineered treatment/resource-recovery processes; UCR geochemical modelling is not the full treatment-plant design course.
Both directly address climate impacts and adaptation; UCR does not include the same engineering-design assessment.
Both directly address the environmental impacts of material use; UCR life-cycle analysis does not supply the complete construction-material-properties curriculum.
Both directly teach calculus for quantitative modelling; the UCR gateway has a broader mathematical-methods remit.
Both directly study linear algebra and matrix/vector methods.
Both directly study numerical mathematical methods, including equation solving and numerical differential equations.
Both directly address differential equations; UCR combines them with multivariable calculus and does not replace the target’s mechanics courses.
Both directly study probability and mathematical statistics.

notes.text: Civil Engineering requires structural, ground and fluid mechanics, construction and transport design alongside water and environmental study. These UCR curricula combine water/environmental science with quantitative modelling or stakeholder/public-economic inquiry. They do not reproduce the full engineering-design and mechanics sequence.
